ClearCoat.what: An array of bright ambience reverbs.
ClearCoat.sound: Dual-mono bright ambiences, the basis of CreamCoat and CrunchCoat.
ClearCoat.use: Bright ambience on albums and mixes.

TapeDelay2.what: A flexible tape echo, rebuilt with undersampling and bandpass tone.
TapeDelay2.sound: Convincing tape wobble when you move the time, with a long delay time.

controls.Time: Delay time. Moving it wobbles like a tape deck.
controls.Freq: Centre frequency of the bandpass in the echoes.

Doublelay.what: StereoDoubler with independent delays and feedback.
Doublelay.sound: Pitch-shifted doubles with a delay tap on each side that can feed back.
Doublelay.use: Widening and doubling vocals and guitars with delay.

controls.Detune: Pitch shift of the doubled left and right.
controls.Delay L: Delay time of the left double.
controls.Delay R: Delay time of the right double.

PitchDelay.what: TapeDelay2 with pitch shift instead of flutter.
PitchDelay.sound: A tape-style echo where time wobble moves but pitch stays, with pitch shift on the echoes.

SampleDelay.what: Three delays in one: milliseconds, samples and subsamples.
SampleDelay.sound: Not quite an echo or timing tool, a little of both. Up to 100 ms, 10 samples, and 1 subsample.
SampleDelay.use: Fine timing adjustments and comb effects.

BrightAmbience3.what: BrightAmbience with undersampling for high sample rates and better feedback.
BrightAmbience3.sound: Bright extruded reverb-like ambience with consistent tone at any rate.

controls.Start: Where in the delay spread the ambience begins.

BrightAmbience2.what: BrightAmbience with better tone and more slapbacky effects.
BrightAmbience2.sound: Prime-number delay taps with stereo spread on centre sounds.

BrightAmbience.what: The classic very bright gated reverb.
BrightAmbience.sound: A big pile of prime-spaced delay taps: nasty but usable. Wet runs hot.

TripleSpread.what: A stereo tripler with extra wideness, from GlitchShifter.
TripleSpread.sound: Three copies: one panned left and pitched down a few cents, one right and up.

controls.Spread: Amount of pitch and stereo spread.

Melt.what: A wobbly, chorusy, weird diffuse effect.
Melt.sound: Reads echoes from a delay buffer and moves them, melting the pitch.

MV2.what: MV adapted to high sample rates.
MV2.sound: Allpass-only bloom with the lo-fi mojo of the Alesis Midiverb.

MV.what: A dual-mono reverb based on BitShiftGain and the old Midiverbs.
MV.sound: Allpass-only bloom with the lo-fi mojo of the Alesis Midiverb.

ADT.what: A double short delay tap with saturation: artificial double-tracking.
ADT.sound: Fixed flanging, as on lots of Beatles tracks, with two taps.

kChamberAR.what: A take on tape echo into chamber echo.
kChamberAR.sound: A wild toy: tape echo feeding a chamber-style space.

StereoChorus.sound: Scales with speed so all settings feel equally intense.

PurestEcho.what: Optimised echo with exactly four evenly spaced taps.
PurestEcho.sound: Precise discrete echoes that stop, with no feedback to muddy the mix.

TapeDelay.what: An old-school tape echo with pitch swerve effects.
TapeDelay.sound: A precursor to Iron Oxide, with tone shaped by clusters of prime-numbered delay taps.

controls.Lean/Ft: Leans the tone lean or fat.

StarChild2.what: A weird digital ambience/echo adapted to high sample rates.
StarChild2.sound: A distinctive, primitive but deep voice that isn't natural.

StarChild.sound: A distinctive voice with nothing to do with naturalness, like old Alesis and Effectron boxes.

Hombre.what: Atmosphere and texture through very short delays.
Hombre.sound: A grease-slide guitar texture inspired by ZZ Top records.

controls.Voicing: Picks the voicing of the delays.

StereoEnsemble.what: A hyperchorus blast from the past.
StereoEnsemble.sound: Ensemble-y goodness with staggered delay pairs for stereo imaging.

StereoDoubler.what: Like GlitchShifter, optimised for pitch-shift doubling and tripling.

controls.Detune: Pitch shift of the doubled voices.

Chorus.what: A mono chorus that also works as a vibrato.
Chorus.sound: A fluid sweep with a gentle lift to the highs.

ChorusEnsemble.what: A more complex, multi-tap mono chorus.
ChorusEnsemble.sound: Rich, textured chorus from a bank of taps. Some settings are deliberately wrong.

Ensemble.what: A weird flangey little modulation effect.

Echojam.what: An echo effect that is secretly a reverb.
Echojam.sound: A strange failed reverb that gathers early delays into a single slapback-like clump, in the manner of Pink Floyd or U2 echoes.
Echojam.use: Guitar echo, or any echo with blurred repeats.
